title: SDK playbook: transient networks, partial tool results & reconciliation
content:
Overview:

This doc is a product/SDK playbook for handling transient network conditions and other flaky client environments when the Hosted API is used with streaming responses and tool-calling. It focuses on: partial/fragmented tool results, resumable sessions, idempotent replays, and ergonomics for client SDKs to make integration robust while keeping server-side semantics simple.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Many mobile and edge clients operate on flaky networks (cell handoffs, airplane mode, captive portals). When clients initiate a streaming call that includes tool invocations (e.g., web search, calendar write), parts of those sequences can fail mid-stream.
- Current hosted-api semantics assume a single reliable TCP connection for the duration of a call. In practice, apps need ways to safely surface partial results, retry or resume operations, and reconcile duplicate tool calls without surprising side effects.
- UX pain: users see half-formed tool outputs or inconsistent app state after a resumed session. Integration complexity pushes teams to avoid streaming or move tool calls client-side.

Goals:
- Provide a minimal protocol and SDK patterns that enable: resumable streams, partial-tool-result envelopes, deduplicated tool call semantics, and clear client-side guidance for backoff and reconnection.
- Keep server guarantees simple: at-most-once tool side-effects unless the customer explicitly opts into at-least-once semantics with idempotency tokens.
- Give product teams default ergonomics that are easy to adopt and safe for common cases.

Non-goals:
- We are not building a full transactional two-phase commit across tool providers. Complex distributed transactions are out of scope.
- We will not change the default server-side tool execution model today; this is SDK/playbook-level behavior and optional config.

User stories (examples):
- Mobile: a user on intermittent LTE starts a chat that triggers a flight-booking toolcall. The connection drops halfway through. On reconnect, the app should receive the latest completed tool outputs and know whether the booking succeeded or needs retry — without double-charging.
- Web app: a productivity extension initiates a multi-step tool flow (summarize -> search -> citation). The client reconnects after a long suspend. Devs want a simple SDK primitive to request the last-known session state and resume streaming from a checkpoint.

Success metrics (proposal):
- Reduce incidents where developers report duplicate tool side-effects in customer apps by 70% in first 6 months after rollout.
- Increase adoption of streaming-enabled SDKs by 2x among early PLG users who sample the SDK.
- Track reconnection-failure rate and time-to-reconcile (metric definitions below).

Constraints and assumptions:
- We assume the platform can persist session checkpoints (small, per-session metadata) for 24 hours by default. Longer retention may be a premium feature.
- Tool providers vary; not all tools are idempotent. SDK patterns must allow caller opt-in for idempotency tokens.
- We will avoid heavy protocol changes to existing streaming endpoints; design should layer on existing websocket/HTTP2 streaming or chunked HTTP responses.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Session coordinator and checkpoints
- When a streaming call begins, the server returns a session_id in the initial handshake frame. This session_id is short-lived (default 24h).
- The server writes lightweight checkpoints at: first tool invocation, tool result completion, and final response completion. Checkpoints contain: session_id, last_event_seq, a summary marker, and stable tool metadata (tool_id, tool_call_id, idempotency_token if provided). These are small opaque blobs persisted in a fast key-value store.

2) Partial-tool-result envelope (frame format)
- Streaming frames include an envelope header to indicate partial payloads and their semantics. Minimal fields (for SDK consumption): frame_seq, session_id, type:[partial|tool-call|tool-result|checkpoint|final], tool_call_id (if applicable), is_final_fragment (bool), checksum/etag (optional).
- Example (human readable):
  -- frame type: tool-result
  -- tool_call_id: t-42
  -- payload: {"status":"in_progress","chunks":["part1..","part2.."]}
  -- is_final_fragment: false

3) Idempotency and deduplication model
- SDKs should expose an optional idempotency_token for tool-invoking requests. If provided, the server stores the token -> tool_call outcome mapping for the session retention window.
- Default platform behavior: if token not provided, server treats tool invocations as at-most-once for a single open connection but may be retried by client SDKs resulting in duplicate execution. SDKs should therefore encourage tokens for any tool with side-effects.

4) Resume semantics and API primitives (SDK-facing)
- resume_session(session_id, last_seq_seen) -> server returns list of missed frames starting after last_seq_seen and latest checkpoint.
- fetch_checkpoint(session_id) -> returns last stable checkpoint metadata for reconciliation.
- safe_invoke_tool(tool_name, params, idempotency_token: optional) -> wrapper that the SDK exposes; it ensures tokens and tracks local pending tool_call_id -> outcome.

5) SDK ergonomics and default behaviors
- SDKs provide two modes: conservative (recommended) and permissive.
  - Conservative: automatically attach idempotency tokens, persist pending tool_call state to local storage, and retry with exponential backoff on reconnect but query checkpoint first to avoid duplicates.
  - Permissive: lightweight behavior that streams frames and surfaces them; minimal local persistence. Use for read-only flows.
- SDKs expose a small reconciler API that app developers can hook into application logic to receive events: on_partial_tool_result(tool_call_id, fragment), on_tool_result(tool_call_id, result), on_reconciled(checkpoint).

6) Backpressure and client-guidance
- Provide SDK utilities to request lower-fidelity streaming in constrained networks: use 'compact_frames' = true hint in handshake to get smaller deltas.
- Clients can signal 'suspend' and 'resume' intents to the server; suspend means server continues producing frames into checkpoint storage but may drop live connection resources. Resume will replay from checkpoint. Consider rate limits on replay.

Observability and telemetry (what we'll capture):
- Metrics to emit: session_start, session_resume, resume_lag_seconds, num_replayed_frames, num_duplicate_tool_detections, idempotency_token_usage_pct, average_reconnects_per_session.
- Traces: attach session_id and tool_call_id to traces for multi-hop debugging.
- Alerts: surge in duplicate tool detections for a customer -> trigger ops and notify product.

Developer experience and docs (SDK docs outline):
- Quickstart: streaming example with safe_invoke_tool wrapper.
- Migration notes: how to add idempotency tokens to existing tool calls.
- Patterns: mobile offline-first example, web-suspend/resume flows, and example server-side webhooks for final tool outcomes.

API Examples (sketches)
- Handshake response (first frame):
  {session_id: "s_1234", server_version: "v2-stream-3", supported_modes: ["compact_frames","checkpoints"]}
- Partial tool-result frame:
  {frame_seq: 42, session_id: "s_1234", type: "tool-result", tool_call_id: "t-42", is_final_fragment: false, payload: "...base64 chunk..."}
- Resume call (SDK):
  POST /v1/sessions/resume {"session_id":"s_1234","after_seq":41} -> returns array of frames up to latest checkpoint.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (labs): SDK experimental flag and opt-in customers. Collect metrics for 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable default SDK conservative mode for new SDK versions; expose server checkpointing for all sessions but retention low (24h).
- Phase 2 (GA): increase retention options, docs + migration guide, and enable console visibility for session replays and duplicate detections.

Open questions / unresolved design tradeoffs:
- Retention window: default 24h is a guess. Should we make it shorter by default to bound storage? Need legal/data retention input.
- Should server provide stronger dedup guarantees (store idempotency tokens globally rather than session-scoped)? That increases storage/lookup costs and cross-region consistency complexity.
- How to present partial tool results in SDKs for typed outputs (JSON schemas) vs raw text streams? We need sample libraries.
- UI-level semantics: when should the app show a provisional result vs wait for confirmed tool completion? Offer guidance in docs, but product teams need to design per-app UIs.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Engineering: spike to implement lightweight checkpoint store and resume API (INF-2345). Owner: Marco. ETA: 3 weeks.
- SDK: prototype conservative_mode in JS and iOS SDKs, add local persistence sample. Owner: Priya. ETA: 4 weeks.
- Docs: short quickstart + migration guide draft. Owner: Evan. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Research: gather top 10 integratees who use tool-calls and ask about current duplicate tool issues. Owner: Lena. ETA: 2 weeks.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative: we prefer to ship SDK guidance and opt-in behavior before changing server guarantees.
- Want feedback on the default conservative vs permissive APIs, and whether the session_id semantics (24h + checkpointing) are acceptable for product teams.
- Related threads: slack/#hosted-api-streaming (link in metadata), INF-2345 ticket contains spike notes.

Appendix: short mobile example flow (sketch)
1) App opens websocket and obtains session_id s_1234.
2) App calls safe_invoke_tool("book_flight", params, idempotency_token="uX-834") -> SDK stores local pending entry {tool_call_id:t-42, token:uX-834} to device storage.
3) Server emits tool-result fragments; SDK calls on_partial_tool_result for UI to show progressive status.
4) Network drops. App reconnects 30s later and calls resume_session(s_1234, after_seq=last_seq_seen).
5) Server returns remaining frames and last checkpoint indicating tool t-42 succeeded. SDK reconciler marks local pending as completed, removes local entry, and invokes on_reconciled(checkpoint).

If the checkpoint had no record but idempotency_token was provided, the SDK asks server to dedupe by token on retry (server may return cached outcome or run the tool if it expired).

-- end of draft --
